spec.title: Do parents of two boys or two girls go on to have a third child more often? A 1980 US census study found 6.8 points more
spec.statement: Angrist and Evans (American Economic Review, 1998) looked at married women aged 21 to 35 in the 1980 US census with two or more children. When the first two children were both boys or both girls, 41.4% went on to have another child, against 34.6% when they were one boy and one girl: 6.8 percentage points more. This runs our own small program on a public copy of the paper's 254,654 women. The rebuild isn't the authors' code, so a mismatch ends as inconclusive.
